scope: Word-recognition implementation and submitted-paper T5 English path. General runtime and HELLO example remain separate. Current explicit-boundary continuous approach only.

diagrams.title: A · General runtime
diagrams.flow:
rOne["R1 · Capture signing (camera)"] --> rTwo["R2 · Extract points and hand details (visual extraction)"]
rTwo --> rThree["R3 · Estimate sign intervals (boundary student)"]
rThree --> rFour["R4 · Identify candidate signs (recognizer)"]
rFour --> rFive["R5 · Select and accept signs (segmental decoder)"]
rFive --> rSix["R6 · Generate English (paper T5 path)"]
rSix --> rSeven["R7 · Finish, display and speak (local output)"]

diagrams.title: B · HELLO walkthrough
diagrams.flow:
hOne["H1 · A person performs HELLO"] --> hTwo["H2 · Extract this movement's points and hand details"]
hTwo --> hThree["H3 · Propose intervals around the movement"]
hThree --> hFour["H4 · Score HELLO and the other vocabulary signs"]
hFour --> hFive["H5 · Accept one HELLO event when evidence is sufficient"]
hFive --> hSix["H6 · Send committed HELLO to T5"]
hSix --> hSeven["H7 · Finish: display and speak the English greeting"]

diagrams.title: C · Isolated-sign training
diagrams.flow:
iOne["I1 · Collect labeled single-sign clips"] --> iTwo["I2 · Preserve training and validation splits"]
iTwo --> iThree["I3 · Prepare landmark and hand-image inputs"]
iThree --> iFour["I4 · Predict with the recognition branches"]
iFour --> iFive["I5 · Measure error (training loss)"]
iFive --> iSix["I6 · Calculate gradients and update trainable weights"]
iSix --> iSeven["I7 · Validate and keep branch checkpoints"]
iSeven --> iEight["I8 · Adapt local examples and train learned fusion"]

diagrams.title: D · Phrase adaptation
diagrams.flow:
pOne["P1 · Load isolated multimodal checkpoint from I8"] --> pFour["P4 · Calculate features using frozen encoders"]
pTwo["P2 · Use annotated phrase recordings"] --> pThree["P3 · Extract one labeled sign segment at a time"]
pThree --> pFour
pFour --> pFive["P5 · Mix phrase-segment features and isolated replay"]
pFive --> pSix["P6 · Update the fusion head with the adaptation loss"]
pSix --> pSeven["P7 · Check phrase and isolated validation"]
pSeven --> pEight["P8 · Keep the phrase-adapted checkpoint"]

diagrams.title: E · Continuous candidate-interval adaptation
diagrams.flow:
cOne["C1 · Load phrase-adapted checkpoint from P8"] --> cFour["C4 · Predict from mixed interval and replay inputs"]
cTwo["C2 · Prepare candidate intervals from phrase evidence"] --> cFour
cThree["C3 · Prepare full, partial and tiny isolated views"] --> cFour
cFour --> cFive["C5 · Combine classification, rejection and retention losses"]
cFive --> cSix["C6 · Update encoders and fusion head carefully"]
cSix --> cSeven["C7 · Check development WER and isolated retention"]
cSeven --> cEight["C8 · Keep primary checkpoint and scoped refinement output"]

diagrams.title: F · Boundary-model training
diagrams.flow:
bOne["B1 · Use matching recordings for both feature pipelines"] --> bTwo["B2 · Run frozen timing teacher on MediaPipe pose"]
bTwo --> bThree["B3 · Align teacher O/B/I targets to timestamps"]
bOne --> bFour["B4 · Build Apple Vision student features"]
bThree --> bFive["B5 · Compare student timing predictions with targets"]
bFour --> bFive
bFive --> bSix["B6 · Update student weights; teacher stays frozen"]
bSix --> bSeven["B7 · Validate timing agreement on held-out videos"]
bSeven --> bEight["B8 · Keep the boundary student for mobile export"]

diagrams.title: G · Paper T5 English training
diagrams.flow:
eOne["E1 · Prepare gloss sequences paired with English targets"] --> eTwo["E2 · Tokenize inputs, targets and masks"]
eTwo --> eThree["E3 · Start from pretrained T5-efficient-tiny"]
eThree --> eFour["E4 · Predict target English tokens (teacher forcing)"]
eFour --> eFive["E5 · Measure token error (cross-entropy)"]
eFive --> eSix["E6 · Backpropagate and update T5 weights"]
eSix --> eSeven["E7 · Keep the recorded checkpoint and evaluate"]
eSeven --> eEight["E8 · Export the paper's gloss-to-English model"]

diagrams.title: H · Checkpoints to mobile runtime
diagrams.flow:
dOne["D1 · Gather selected checkpoints and label maps"] --> dTwo["D2 · Define model input and output contracts"]
dTwo --> dThree["D3 · Convert graphs to Core ML"]
dThree --> dFour["D4 · Compare converted outputs with source outputs"]
dFour --> dFive["D5 · Bundle models and decoder configuration"]
dFive --> dSix["D6 · Load and warm models on the device"]
dSix --> dSeven["D7 · Run the general pipeline R1 to R7"]
dSeven --> dEight["D8 · Measure device behavior and keep evaluation scopes clear"]

runtime.intro: The main sequence is deliberately simple. Read each card's INPUT FROM line to see reused evidence; an arrow does not mean that all data comes only from the immediately previous step. Word-recognition scope; English follows the submitted paper's T5 description.
cards: R1 · Capture signing

INPUT FROM: device camera.
DO: receive upright, unmirrored BGRA frames and their timestamps. Current iPhone LIVE requests 1280×720, with 640×480 fallback; processing targets 20 positions/s.
OUTPUT: pixel buffer + elapsed seconds + image dimensions.
USED BY: R2. Only the front-camera preview is mirrored.
R2 · Extract visual information

INPUT FROM: R1 frames.
DO: Apple Vision extracts 61 selected hand, face and upper-body points; make left-hand, right-hand and union crops. Encode valid 256×256 RGB crops using MobileCLIP2-S0.
OUTPUT: timestamped points/confidence; cached [3,512] appearance features, validity [3], boxes [3,4].
USED BY: BOTH R3 and R4. The image encoder runs once per processed frame, not once per candidate.
R3 · Estimate intervals

INPUT FROM: R2 landmark observations, not hand-image embeddings.
DO: derive 450 geometry/motion/presence/confidence features. The boundary student reads [1,64,450] plus [1,64] validity and predicts outside/beginning/inside (O/B/I), with six-position lookahead. Candidate proposals use this timing evidence.
OUTPUT: O/B/I timing scores and proposed [start,end] intervals.
USED BY: BOTH R4 and R5. This stage does not name the sign.
R4 · Recognize each candidate

INPUT FROM: R2 points AND cached hand features, selected using R3 intervals.
DO: trim/normalize the span; resample landmarks to [32,61,5], select 16 image times → [16,3,512], plus validity [16,3] and boxes [16,3,4]. Part-wise/global landmark and temporal hand branches feed learned fusion.
OUTPUT: 100 vocabulary logits per candidate; derive normalized scores with softmax.
USED BY: R5. Export batch eight means eight candidate slots, not eight simultaneous signs.
R5 · Select and commit

INPUT FROM: R3 timing + R4 recognition scores + R2 motion evidence.
DO: score whole intervals; semi-Markov search selects an ordered, non-overlapping path. Stability and repetition rules determine when results become committed.
OUTPUT: accepted gloss, score, event interval and commit time, stored in the gloss buffer.
USED BY: R6. A high score alone is insufficient; preview is still provisional.
R6 · Generate English

INPUT FROM: committed gloss sequence and scores from R5; trained T5 from E8 via deployment D3–D5.
DO: encode gloss evidence and generate English incrementally; retain completed sentences after consistency checks. Token inputs/masks [1,64]; encoder hidden states [1,64,256].
OUTPUT: provisional English; Finish finalizes the remaining text.
USED BY: R7. This is the PAPER English path, not an assertion about another English implementation.
R7 · Finish, display and speak

INPUT FROM: Finish control + pending R3–R5 evidence + R6 English.
DO: flush unresolved timing/decoding first; send any newly committed tail to R6, then finalize English. Display the final message and use local text-to-speech.
OUTPUT: English text and audio; session history where enabled by the app.
NEXT: reset utterance state. Finish does not guarantee that recognition or translation errors are corrected.
runtime.source: Paper: §3.2, §4.6.1–4.6.2, printed pp.75–82. Code supplement: LiveReelCore.swift; LiveReelModels.swift; LiveReelEngine.swift; LiveReelDecoder.swift; LiveReelStage3.swift. Shapes/settings describe their verified contracts; English is explicitly the paper path.

hello.intro: A separate worked example of R1–R7. This illustrates the intended flow; it is not a newly measured HELLO replay, and no confidence score or time interval is invented.
cards: H1 · The camera sees HELLO

CORRESPONDS TO: R1.
INPUT FROM: the signer performs one HELLO event in front of the camera.
DO: capture the movement over successive timestamps, including surrounding rest.
OUTPUT TO H2: frames containing that event. The system has not yet identified HELLO.
H2 · Extract evidence

CORRESPONDS TO: R2.
INPUT FROM: H1 frames.
DO: detect point locations and crop visible hands. Cache each frame's hand embeddings.
OUTPUT TO H3 AND H4: the same timestamped landmark and appearance evidence. Landmarks describe geometry; appearance features can supply hand-detail information.
H3 · Propose possible intervals

CORRESPONDS TO: R3.
INPUT FROM: H2 landmarks.
DO: estimate where activity begins and continues. Several overlapping intervals may describe the same HELLO movement.
OUTPUT TO H4 AND H5: candidate intervals and timing scores. Three proposals do not mean the signer performed three signs.
H4 · Score the candidates

CORRESPONDS TO: R4.
INPUT FROM: H2 visual evidence selected by H3 intervals.
DO: form the 32-time landmark tensor and 16-time hand tensor for each candidate. Compare the resulting learned representation against the 100-class output space.
OUTPUT TO H5: each candidate's HELLO score and alternative-class scores. Recognizer confidence is not validation accuracy.
H5 · Accept one event

CORRESPONDS TO: R5.
INPUT FROM: H3 timing + H4 scores + H2 movement evidence.
DO: compare compatible interval sequences and wait for sufficient stability. Overlapping HELLO predictions can refer to one event.
ILLUSTRATIVE OUTPUT TO H6: one committed HELLO, with its score and timestamps. The decoder can still make errors; this example assumes correct acceptance.
H6 · Render the greeting

CORRESPONDS TO: R6.
INPUT FROM: the committed HELLO in H5, not provisional H4 predictions.
DO: the paper's T5 path renders English from the accumulated gloss evidence.
ILLUSTRATIVE OUTPUT TO H7: an English greeting such as “Hello.” Exact wording is not a measured output of this walkthrough.
H7 · Complete the message

CORRESPONDS TO: R7.
INPUT FROM: Finish plus H6 text and any pending recognition tail.
DO: flush, finalize the English and display/speak the result locally.
OUTPUT: the greeting as text and speech. The GENERAL diagram remains separate and still covers any in-vocabulary word.
hello.source: Teaching example mapped to general steps R1–R7; shapes are actual input contracts, while the successful HELLO event and English greeting are illustrative. No new camera test or evaluation was run.

isolated.intro: This trains recognition of a labeled single-sign clip. It is different from training timing or English. After each optimizer update, repeat prediction/loss/update on the next training batch; validation does not backpropagate.
cards: I1–I2 · Data and separation

INPUT FROM: admitted isolated-sign datasets and their class labels; 100-word label map.
DO: preserve official signer-disjoint Citizen splits and applicable source identities. Separate train from validation; do not tune on the protected test set.
OUTPUT TO I3: labeled training and validation memberships. One example has one sign label, unlike an unsegmented phrase.
I3 · Prepare model inputs

INPUT FROM: I2 single-sign clips.
DO: extract/normalize landmarks, preserve missing-data flags, resample 32 times; obtain pretrained MobileCLIP2 appearance features at 16 times and three views.
OUTPUT TO I4: [B,32,61,5], [B,16,3,512], [B,16,3] validity and [B,16,3,4] boxes, plus target class IDs.
TRAIN ONLY: augmentation and balanced class sampling; validation uses its fixed evaluation preparation.
I4 · Branch predictions

INPUT FROM: I3 tensors.
DO: landmark branch processes four anatomical regions at width 64, combines them at width 256, then uses four global blocks/eight heads. Hand temporal branch uses three blocks/eight heads, width 256.
OUTPUT TO I5: branch class logits and pooled embeddings.
LEARNED: feature projections, temporal blocks, pooling and classifiers; the pretrained crop encoder supplies cached appearance features.
I5 · Loss, in proper steps

INPUT FROM: I4 logits + the correct I3 class.
1. Softmax converts logits into a class distribution.
2. Cross-entropy compares prediction with the target: L=−Σ y_k log p_k, where y is the target distribution and p is the model distribution.
3. Base label smoothing ε=0.1 softens targets; it does not change the correct class.
OUTPUT TO I6: a differentiable training loss. Accuracy alone does not provide the same smooth gradient signal.
I6 · Update weights

INPUT FROM: I5 loss and the active model parameters.
1. Backpropagation computes gradients ∂L/∂w.
2. The optimizer uses gradients to update trainable weights after each batch.
CODE SUPPLEMENT, BASE: AdamW, peak LR 3×10⁻⁴, eight warm-up epochs then cosine decay, w eight decay 0.03. LR scales the update; it is not a class probability.
OUTPUT: new weights for the next training batch.
I7 · Check generalization

INPUT FROM: trained I6 branch checkpoints + held-out I2 validation clips.
DO: evaluate without w eight updates; select the recorded checkpoint under that stage's rule.
PAPER: base study recorded 130 epochs; selected epoch 100 reached 96.83% base validation accuracy.
OUTPUT TO I8: selected branch weights. This is a base-study result, not the accuracy of every later component or the complete camera-to-English system.
I8 · Replay and fusion

INPUT FROM: I7 landmark checkpoint, trained hand temporal branch and isolated examples.
DO: the selected lineage includes mild-roll local replay, then a learned fusion head using frozen branch features/scores. Replay peak LR 5×10⁻⁵ is a later adaptation rate, not the original base rate.
OUTPUT TO P1: isolated multimodal checkpoint.
FUSION: 0.75/0.25 normalized-score baseline + a learned gated residual, rather than only averaging.
Class sampling and regularization

ORIGIN: I3 training batches.
Balanced class sampling changes how often examples are drawn, not automatically how severely their mistakes are penalized. Replacement means a clip can repeat and another can be unseen in one epoch.
Dropout masks activations during training; w eight decay shrinks parameters; EMA maintains averaged weights. EMA does not clip gradients. These mechanisms help retention/generalization but still require validation.
isolated.source: Paper: recognition development, Table10, printed pp.78–79,93–94. Code supplements: train_stage_1_v17.py; model_v17.py; train_stage_1_hand_mobileclip2_v17.py; train_unified_multimodal_student_v17.py. Base LR verified in stage1-architecture log2026-10-19; ancestry in paper_checkpoint_lineage_v17_20261013/REPORT.md.

phrase.intro: Phrase adaptation still teaches single-sign classification: it extracts individually annotated signs from connected signing. It still predicts individual sign identities.
cards: P1 · Starting weights

INPUT FROM: I8 isolated multimodal checkpoint.
DO: initialize the recognizer with already learned branch encoders and fusion weights.
OUTPUT TO P4/P6: starting encoders and fusion head. Fine-tuning starts from prior weights rather than starting again from random weights.
P2–P3 · Obtain labeled segments

INPUT FROM: approved phrase recordings and per-sign start/end annotations.
DO: take the interval assigned to one gloss. Preserve its surrounding-sign context in the original recording; prepare the model inputs from the admitted segment views.
OUTPUT TO P4: one sign segment and its label. A phrase containing several signs supplies several annotated segments; these are not independent signers.
P4 · Calculate frozen features

INPUT FROM: P3 segments + P1 encoders.
DO: run the landmark and hand encoders to calculate embeddings and branch scores. Encoder weights are frozen in the saved phrase phase.
OUTPUT TO P5: cached branch features/logits and labels.
FROZEN DOES NOT MEAN OFF: calculations continue; gradients do not update these encoder weights.
P5 · Add isolated replay

INPUT FROM: P4 phrase features + earlier isolated examples/features from I3/I8.
DO: mix the two views so adaptation also sees earlier vocabulary behavior.
OUTPUT TO P6: mixed training batches.
WHY: the fusion head still changes, so its decisions can drift even when encoders are frozen. Replay constrains the trainable part's behavior.
P6 · Learn the fusion change

INPUT FROM: P5 mixed batch + frozen reference predictions from the starting model.
DO: calculate class cross-entropy, the configured confusable-pair term, replay KL retention and parameter anchoring. Backpropagate through the trainable fusion head.
OUTPUT: updated fusion parameters; encoder parameters remain unchanged.
SOURCE MECHANISM: AdamW and cosine scheduling; do not borrow an unverified exact starting LR from a different phase.
P7–P8 · Validate and retain

INPUT FROM: P6 candidates + phrase and isolated development sets.
DO: assess phrase-segment recognition alongside isolated retention; preserve the saved selection rule.
CODE SUPPLEMENT: saved phrase checkpoint has frozen encoders and selected epoch 21.
OUTPUT TO C1: phrase-adapted checkpoint. It learns from signs embedded in phrases; it does not generate English.
Connection to runtime

TRAINING OUTPUT: P8 is a parent checkpoint for C1, not a standalone additional camera stage.
RUNTIME PURPOSE: signs in connected signing may start/end away from the resting poses common in isolated clips. Adapting to those views can help recognition.
LIMIT: this purpose does not prove perfect boundary tolerance; candidate-interval training and end-to-end evaluation still matter.
phrase.source: Paper: printed pp.79,93–94. Source: train_unified_phrase_adapt_v17.py:cached frozen-encoder features, losses and head update. Saved phase metadata/lineage: run_v2/phrase_adapt and paper_checkpoint_lineage_v17_20261013/REPORT.md. No new training is authorized or launched.

interval.intro: This is the current explicit-boundary approach to connected signing. The recognizer learns candidate-interval behavior; the boundary student learns timing separately, and the segmental decoder performs search rather than gradient training.
cards: C1–C2 · Parent and interval data

INPUT FROM: P8 weights and admitted phrase annotations/candidate-interval supervision derived from P2/P3.
DO: construct views resembling the intervals R3 may propose, including boundary variation and transitions.
OUTPUT TO C4: interval tensors and sign targets.
PURPOSE: improve recognition on runtime-like inputs, not merely on neatly trimmed isolated clips.
C3 · Three replay views

INPUT FROM: earlier isolated training clips from I3.
FULL: keep the original sign label and earlier prediction as eligible retention evidence.
PARTIAL: shorten a sign but keep the parent label for the eligible partial view.
TINY FRAGMENT: train toward a flat distribution over existing 100 classes to discourage a confident guess.
OUTPUT TO C4: tensors plus the appropriate supervision type; no extra rest-word class is added.
C4–C5 · Combine the losses

INPUT FROM: predictions on C2/C3 and a frozen reference model initialized from C1.
1. Class cross-entropy supervises eligible labeled inputs.
2. Tiny fragments receive a flat-target penalty.
3. Applicable full isolated replay receives KL retention at temperature 2.
4. Parameter anchoring discourages drift from starting weights.
OUTPUT TO C6: total loss. Partial/rejection views are excluded from whole-clip reference retention.
C6 · Which weights change?

INPUT FROM: C5 gradients.
SELECTED PRIMARY RUN: encoders are NOT frozen; encoder LR 1×10⁻⁵ and fusion-head LR 2×10⁻⁵. AdamW decay 0.001; cosine schedule; gradient-norm clipping 1.
CODE SUPPLEMENT: clipping limits the gradient norm before the optimizer step, not confidence or the exact final parameter-update norm.
OUTPUT: adapted branch encoders and fusion head. This differs from frozen-encoder P6.
C7 · Choose under both objectives

INPUT FROM: C6 checkpoints + connected-signing development evaluation + isolated validation.
DO: minimize development WER subject to isolated retention floors.
CODE SUPPLEMENT: eight planned epochs; selected primary epoch 4.
OUTPUT TO C8: accepted primary checkpoint. A later epoch or a higher isolated percentage alone is not automatically preferable.
C8 · Primary and refinement

INPUT FROM: C7 primary, plus separately reviewed transition examples for scoped refinement.
DO: preserve the primary output while keeping an additional adapted fusion output for guarded transition evidence. The refinement phase freezes encoders; do not apply that statement backward to C6.
OUTPUT TO D1/R4: primary recognition and conditional refinement evidence.
The two interval variants share a phrase parent; one is not assumed to descend from the other.
Loss formula and settings

SOURCE-ONLY OBJECTIVE: L=L_class+0.5 × L_flat+L_retain+0.01 × L_anchor, with terms applied only to eligible rows; retention uses KL at T=2 and factor T².
Recorded partial probability 0.30, retained fraction≥0.25; tiny-fragment probability 0.15 on eligible non-partial replay, fraction 0.10–0.25.
These are conditional sampling rules, not two unconditional percentages of all clips. They are implementation supplements, not new paper results.
interval.source: Paper: printed pp.79,93–94. Source: train_span_recognizer_v17.py:fragment/reject masks, parameter groups, loss and selection; selected run_frag25_reject history/checkpoint metadata. Refinement: confidence_training_recipe.json and train_confidence.py; current primary/guarded use in LiveReelModels.swift.

boundary.intro: The timing teacher and the ASL recognizer are different models. This diagram trains the O/B/I timing student used at R3; it does not train the 100 sign labels.
cards: B1 · Matching recordings

INPUT FROM: admitted videos with both teacher-pose and Apple raw-observation caches.
DO: preserve recording identity and timestamps. Exclude the protected test/tuning and specified validation groups from training.
OUTPUT TO B2/B4: two representations of the SAME recording; this is how teacher targets can be aligned with student observations.
B2–B3 · Frozen teacher targets

INPUT FROM: B1 MediaPipe pose sequence.
DO: run the pretrained German Sign Language timing teacher; derive outside/beginning/inside distributions and align them to student timestamps.
OUTPUT TO B5: soft O/B/I targets q, not ASL vocabulary names.
TEACHER WEIGHTS: unchanged. Soft uncertainty is evidence from the teacher, not deliberately wrong answers to make learning harder.
B4 · Student inputs

INPUT FROM: B1 Apple Vision raw observations.
DO: build 450 geometry/motion/presence/confidence features per position and 64-position windows with a validity mask.
OUTPUT TO B5: [B,64,450], valid [B,64].
STUDENT: width 256, four Transformer layers, eight heads; six-position runtime lookahead. These dimensions are source supplements to the paper's four-layer description.
B5 · Compare timing distributions

INPUT FROM: B3 target q and B4 student prediction p.
1. Student produces three O/B/I logits per selected window position.
2. Log-softmax gives log p.
3. Soft-target cross-entropy: L=−mean Σ q_k log p_k.
OUTPUT TO B6: student loss. The word recognizer's class labels are not needed for this distribution-matching objective.
B6 · Update the student

INPUT FROM: B5 training loss.
DO: backpropagate through the student; clip gradient norm and update its trainable weights. The compatible trainer uses AdamW and OneCycle scheduling.
OUTPUT TO B7: candidate student checkpoints.
The teacher still provides targets without w eight updates. Exact command overrides must be verified before quoting a particular training LR as selected.
B7–B8 · Select timing model

INPUT FROM: student checkpoints + separate held-out-video teacher/student pairs.
DO: compare timing distributions using KL; the checked trainer selects its lowest held-out KL.
OUTPUT TO D1, THEN R3: selected Apple-input boundary student.
This measures timing imitation, not 100-class recognition accuracy. Teacher training language does not make the student a German-to-ASL translator.
boundary.source: Paper: printed pp.78–79 and §4.6.2. Source: train_av_boundary_v17.py:teacher_obi, aligned, train/validation exclusions, soft-target loss and KL selection; av_boundary_v17.py. Teacher and student representations are aligned by recording and time.

english.intro: Only the submitted paper's T5 English path is covered here. It learns a text-to-text mapping, rather than learning sign recognition from camera pixels.
cards: E1 · Training pairs

INPUT FROM: the prepared gloss-to-English corpus; each row supplies glosses, confidence evidence and a target English rendering.
DO: preserve its train/validation memberships and hold out evaluation sessions.
OUTPUT TO E2: text pairs. A target is supervision, not proof that every English rendering is linguistically perfect.
This corpus preparation is separate from extracting landmark/image tensors.
E2 · Token preparation

INPUT FROM: E1 pairs.
DO: encode each gloss with its confidence bucket and tokenize the English target. Prepare input IDs, attention masks and target IDs; mask target padding with −100 so it contributes no token loss.
OUTPUT TO E3/E4: integer tensors [B,L], with recorded length buckets 24/40/64.
For the mobile export, L=64. Tokens are not necessarily whole words.
E3–E4 · Fine-tune T5

INPUT FROM: pretrained T5-efficient-tiny plus E2 tensors.
DO: encoder reads the gloss evidence; during training, the decoder receives the shifted correct target prefix and predicts the next English token (teacher forcing).
OUTPUT TO E5: token logits [B,L,V], where V is tokenizer vocabulary size.
PAPER MODEL: about 15.6M parameters. Exported encoder hidden states are [1,64,256].
E5–E6 · Token loss and update

INPUT FROM: E4 logits + E2 target IDs.
1. Calculate cross-entropy for non-padding target tokens.
2. Backpropagate that loss through T5.
3. Update trainable parameters using Adafactor.
RECORDED RECIPE, CODE SUPPLEMENT: batch 32, peak LR 3×10⁻⁴,100 warm-up steps then linear decay toward 10%, FP32, gradient clipping 1. Repeat across training batches.
E7 · Recorded checkpoint rule

INPUT FROM: E6 final checkpoint and validation text pairs.
DO: keep the final step of the recorded bounded run; validation loss was reported, not used to select its best epoch.
PAPER: validation loss 0.2515 at optimizer step 4,539.
Evaluate English separately from recognizer accuracy/WER. Overlap scores and automated judgments do not replace independent human assessment of faithfulness.
E8 · Connect training to runtime

INPUT FROM: E7 T5 checkpoint + tokenizer/metadata.
OUTPUT TO D1–D5: encoder and decoder-step exports, both parts of one English model.
USED AT R6: inference generates tokens autoregressively using its own generated prefix. Unlike training, the correct target sentence is not supplied at runtime.
The English model cannot enlarge the recognizer's 100-sign visual vocabulary.
english.source: Paper: printed p.81, §4.8 translation results, validation loss0.2515/step4,539. Matching code/receipts: train_stage3_multisentence_v17.py; stage3_multisentence_bakeoff_v17_20260929/tiny/recipe.json and targeted training_result fields; export_stage3_t5_coreml_v17.py.

deployment.intro: Training produces checkpoints; deployment makes them usable by the app. Conversion is not another training phase, and this board's English contract remains the paper's T5 path.
cards: D1 · Gather selected outputs

INPUT FROM: I8/P8/C8 recognizer lineage, B8 boundary student and E8 T5, plus the pretrained crop encoder and 100-word label map.
DO: pin the selected checkpoints and their metadata. C8 is the word-recognition output used here; earlier parents are provenance, not extra sequential runtime models.
OUTPUT TO D2: a defined set of model components.
D2 · Pin the contracts

INPUT FROM: D1 models + preparation code.
RECOGNIZER: [8,32,61,5], [8,16,3,512], [8,16,3], [8,16,3,4] → word logits [8,100]. Short candidate batches repeat the last input into unused slots; ignore unused outputs.
BOUNDARY: [1,64,450] plus validity → [1,3].
T5: token/mask [1,64] → hidden [1,64,256] → next-token decoding.
D3 · Export compatible graphs

INPUT FROM: D2 contracts and selected weights.
DO: convert to Core ML for the mobile runtime. Selected visual/recognition graphs use FP16; the paper T5 encoder and decoder exports use FP32.
OUTPUT TO D4: exported graph packages.
The recognizer package does not contain the crop encoder, boundary model, translator or system speech engine.
D4 · Check conversion effects

INPUT FROM: D3 exports + source model outputs on matching inputs.
DO: compare logits/predictions and evaluate the relevant held-out or development contract. Equal total accuracy alone does not establish identical per-example predictions.
OUTPUT TO D5: verified export evidence, not an assumption that lower precision is behaviorally identical. No new evaluation is run to draw this diagram.
D5–D6 · Integrate and warm

INPUT FROM: D4 exports, label/token maps and decoder settings.
DO: bundle assets, load them through the app's model interfaces and warm graph execution. Engine processing and English work use separate queues; UI updates run on the main thread.
OUTPUT TO R2/R3/R4/R6: loaded inference components.
Segmental decoding is runtime search/configuration, not a separate learned neural checkpoint.
D7–D8 · Operate and measure

INPUT FROM: the complete R1–R7 path on the target phone.
DO: measure recognition/sequence behavior and device latency, memory and sustained performance with clear boundaries.
OUTPUT: deployment evidence. Package bytes measure storage, not runtime RAM or compute. The paper's 31.14ms extraction-to-recognizer measurement is not full camera-to-speech delay.
No weights are trained during ordinary inference.
deployment.source: Paper: prototype/export/performance sections. Source: export_dual_confidence.py; export_stage3_t5_coreml_v17.py; LiveReelModels.swift; retained T5 interface LiveReelStage3.swift. Recognition/timing implementation and paper T5 are deliberately scoped, not claimed as an audit of every current app subsystem.
